title: Corey Haines's referral and affiliate playbook: design, incentives, and when to build virality instead
summary: An AI-agent skill Corey wrote on designing referral and affiliate programs. It covers when to engineer virality into the product, how to pick trigger moments and incentive structures, how to optimize and measure a program, and where affiliates fit.

principles.text: Check if virality can be built into the product before building a reward-driven referral program, but don't force it where it doesn't fit.
principles.quote: Before building a reward-driven program, check whether virality can be **built into the product** — often cheaper and more durable than paid referrals. But **don't force virality where it doesn't naturally fit.**

principles.text: Collaboration, communication, and output-producing products are naturally viral; backend or internal tools should lean on referral, content, and partnerships.
principles.quote: **Natural** (build for it): collaboration tools, communication tools, user-facing outputs — every use exposes the product to non-users.

principles.text: Ask for referrals at high-intent moments: the aha moment, a milestone, great support, or a renewal or upgrade.
Reward at the aha moment or milestone, not signup, and lead with the bigger-feeling number.
principles.quote: Reward at the **aha moment or milestone**, not signup.

principles.text: Rank share mechanisms by friction: in-product sharing converts best, then personalized links, email, social, and codes.
Use affiliates to reach audiences you don't have, especially for higher-ticket products that can afford commissions.
principles.quote: Reaching audiences you don't have access to
